lesson 1.lesson prompt: Create the first lesson readings called "What is HCI?" that contains pages that teach students about "The definition of Human-Computer Interaction" and "what HCI includes in day-to-day activities (e.g., human psychology and cognition in relation to technology).", the content should be engaging and long enough to be considered a full lesson. The content should also include images and examples to help the students understand the material better. Ignore including things for the professor to use to teach the lesson, such as lecture notes or a presentation. Just create the readings for the students to read and learn from. The readings should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 1_lesson.html".
lesson 1.quiz prompt: The module will also include 1 quiz that contains 10 multiple choice questions.
lesson 1.assignment prompt: There will be an assignment that calls for the students to fill out a syllabus agreement survey and direct them to join a group for the group presentation and project assignment due at the end of the semester. Do not add "join a group" to the rubric, as if they do not join one willingly, they will be assigned to one. Do not add the extra deliverables to the "join a group," as groups are built into the class and do not need proof of joining a group. Keep the "join a group" deliverable to remind the student to join a group, else they'll be put into a random group. Only provide instructions for the syllabus agreement survey and joining a group, as well as a rubric for the syllabus agreement survey. The assignment should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 1_assignment.html". Keep the assignment a certain length so that it does break the string index limit, but also so that it is long enough to be considered a full assignment. The assignment should also be engaging and informative for the students, and should effectively convey the importance of the syllabus agreement and joining a group for the class.

lesson 2.lesson prompt: Create the second lesson readings "Intro to Psychology Applied in HCI." Students will learn about human perception and cognition in relation to technology. They will also learn about UI design guidelines, the content should be engaging and long enough to be considered a full lesson. The content should also include images and examples to help the students understand the material better. Ignore including things for the professor to use to teach the lesson, such as lecture notes or a presentation. Just create the readings for the students to read and learn from. The readings should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 2_lesson.html".
lesson 2.quiz prompt: The module will also include 1 quiz that contains 10 multiple choice questions.
lesson 2.assignment prompt: The students will also have an assignment called "Website Analysis" where the students will look at a website of their choice and analyze it based on the lesson, which included human perception and cognition in relation to technology and UI guidelines. Only provide instructions for the assignment and a rubric for the assignment. The assignment should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 2_assignment.html". The assignment should be engaging and informative for the students, and should effectively convey the importance of analyzing websites based on the material learned in the lesson. The assignment should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 1_assignment.html". Keep the assignment a certain length so that it does break the string index limit, but also so that it is long enough to be considered a full assignment. The assignment should also be engaging and informative for the students, and should effectively convey the importance of analyzing websites based on the material learned in the lesson.

lesson 3.lesson prompt: Create the third lesson readings called "Designing for User Experience." Students will learn about user-centered design principles and how to apply them in real-world scenarios, the content should be engaging and long enough to be considered a full lesson. The content should also include images and examples to help the students understand the material better. Ignore including things for the professor to use to teach the lesson, such as lecture notes or a presentation. Just create the readings for the students to read and learn from. The readings should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 3_lesson.html".
lesson 3.quiz prompt: The module will also include 1 quiz that contains 10 multiple choice questions.
lesson 3.assignment prompt: The students will also have a coding lab that through a set of instructions telling them what to do, but not how to do it, take a unformatted web page and "fix" it using visual design principles. Create a HTML page that is unformatted for the students to fix. Create the same HTML page with a CSS page that makes it formatted as a solution. Give hints for each part of the unformatted page to help the students know which visual design principle they should apply to that part (e.g., if a button element needs moves, give them hints about flexbox and grid CSS). The assignment should be in HTML format, and should be saved as "lesson 3_assignment.html". The assignment should be engaging and informative for the students, and should effectively convey the importance of applying visual design principles to create a better user experience. The assignment should also be long enough to be considered a full assignment, but not too long that it breaks the string index limit.

lesson 4.lesson prompt: Create the fourth lesson readings, "Gestalt Principles and Visual Perception" Students will learn: What each of the Gestalt Principles are and how to apply the gestalt principles to interfaces (in-depth).
lesson 4.quiz prompt: The module will also include 1 quiz that contains 10 multiple choice questions.
lesson 4.assignment prompt: The students will also have an assignment called "Determining Gestalt Principles" where the students will look at images of gestalt principles and will have to determine which gestalt principle it is." Generate example images of whatever Gestalt Principles are going to be used. DO NOT USE WORDS to allow students to figure which principle it is themselves. Generate 4-5 different examples for the assignment.

lesson 5.lesson prompt: Create the fifth lesson readings "UI/UX Design." Students will learn how to differentiate between User Interface and User Experience design, learn why both matter to design as a whole, and learn the design process (Empathize, Define, Iterate, etc.).
lesson 5.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 5.assignment prompt: They will also have an assignment called determining good vs bad design. The assignment requires the students to use the knowledge they got from this lesson, as well as the previous lesson on UI design guidelines and the Gestalt Principles to determine whether the designs they see are considered to be good or bad designs.

lesson 6.lesson prompt: Create the sixth lesson readings "UI/UX Design." Students will learn how to differentiate between User Interface and User Experience design, learn why both matter to design as a whole, and learn the design process (Empathize, Define, Iterate, etc.).
lesson 6.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 6.assignment prompt: The students will also have an Assignment where the students read a article found on the web about an emerging piece of technology and discuss how the piece of technology may change interaction design.

lesson 7.lesson prompt: Create the seventh lesson readings "Low-Fidelity Prototypes." The students will learn what Low-Fidelity Prototypes are (with examples), benefits of using low-fidelity prototypes, and comparisons to high-fidelity prototypes.
lesson 7.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 7.assignment prompt: The students will also complete an assignment which requires each group to create 5 to 7 low-fidelity prototypes for each idea for features they get for their final project.

lesson 8.lesson prompt: Create the eighth lesson readings "User Research Part 1." The students will learn SOME of the different types of research techniques (such as interviews, surveys, and contextual inquiries). The students will also learn in more detail about these research techniques and how to use them effectively.
lesson 8.quiz prompt: The students will take a 50 multiple-choice question midterm based on this and previous lessons.
lesson 8.assignment prompt: The students will also be assigned to doing one contextual inquiry, as well as gathering and analyzing data based on their contextual inquiries that is based on their group's final project assignment.

lesson 9.lesson prompt: Create the ninth lesson readings: "User Research Part 2." Students will learn what user journeys and personas are, as well as other techniques.
lesson 9.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 9.assignment prompt: The students will also have an assignment that requires the students to create one Journey Map and one Persona to ensure their understanding of each research technique.

lesson 10.lesson prompt: Create the tenth lesson readings "Figma/High-Fidelity Prototype." The students will learn what a high-fidelity prototype is, a reiteration of the comparison between low and high fidelity prototypes, and a workshop of Figma. For the Figma workshop, it will discuss the very basics of how to make a wireframe, how to use design templates, and how to make and use components.
lesson 10.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz based on the lesson.
lesson 10.assignment prompt: The students will also have to complete an assignment that requires the students, within their group, to create a high-fidelity prototype using Figma. The students will also use their low-fidelity prototypes and their contextual inquiries to influence their high-fidelity prototype.

lesson 11.lesson prompt: Create the eleventh lesson readings, "Usability Tests." Students will learn: What usability testing is, the difference between moderated and unmoderated usability testing, and how to efficiently conduct each type of usability test.
lesson 11.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 11.assignment prompt: The students will also have an Assignment that requires each group to perform twice as many usability tests as there are group members (1 of each kind person person). For moderated usability testing specifically, two students will test 1 participant (one as the tester, the other as the note taker).

lesson 12.lesson prompt: Create the twelfth lesson readings, "Accessibility and Inclusive Design." Students will learn: Different types of inclusive/accessibility features, such as alt text in images and dark mode, as well as how to implement them (e.g., using @media to create a dark mode).
lesson 12.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 12.assignment prompt: The students will also have a coding lab that requires the students to “fix” a website page by including accessibility and inclusive features (e.g., alt text in images and dark mode).

lesson 13.lesson prompt: Create the thirteenth lesson readings, "Emerging Technologies." Students will learn: Artificial Intelligence in UX (which will help lead into ethics (next lesson)), Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, Smart Environments, Internet of Things, and Future trends in HCI.
lesson 13.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 13.assignment prompt: The students will also have an assignment where the students are required to read a provided article and discuss how this piece of technology may change interaction design.

lesson 14.lesson prompt: Create the fourteenth lesson readings, "Ethics in HCI and Emerging Technologies" Students will learn:Dark patterns, persuasive technology, privacy concerns, bias in technology, ethical responsibilities of designers, and trust and transparency.
lesson 14.quiz prompt: The students will take a 10 multiple choice question quiz about this lesson.
lesson 14.assignment prompt: The students will also have an assignment where the students will be required to read 1 or 2 shorter ethical case studies and write their answers to a prompt, while also responding to 2 other responses from other students.

lesson 15.final presentation prompt: Create the final presentation assignment and rubric. For the final presentation, the students are required to get with their groups and create a final presentation that consists of their designs (including a demo), research process, and implementation that they worked on across the semester, showing what they learned from this HCI class.

lesson 16.final exam prompt: Create the final exam for an HCI class. The final exam will have 75 questions. The questions within the final exam should include: What is HCI?, Psychology Applied in HCI, Visual Design Principles, Gestalt Principles and Visual Perceptions, UI/UX Design, Information Architecture and User Flows, Low-Fidelity Prototypes, User Research, Figma and High-Fidelity Prototypes, Usability Testing, Accessibility and inclusive design, Emerging Technologies, and Ethics in HCI and Emerging Technologies. Keep the same amount of questions for each topic as close as possible.
